newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin stays in bed with cold, under treatment.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin stays in bed with cold, under treatment.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who is suffering from a cold, was under doctors' orders to take things easy on Tuesday and spend plenty of time in bed at his country residence near Moscow, a Kremlin spokesman said.
"The president will spend today at his residence at Gorky-9, most probably with his family," he told Reuters. "He will be partially confined to bed."

The spokesman said Yeltsin, who on Monday cancelled meetings for the next few days, was following an "intensive course of treatment" but could give no details of his illness or what medication he was taking. He added, however, that doctors saw no need for Yeltsin to go into hospital.

Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Monday the president had a heavy cold and a temperature but that the illness had no relation to the 65-year-old Kremlin leader's recent heart bypass surgery.
Yeltsin had a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5 and returned to work at the end of last year.
Veteran Texan heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised on the operation, told Reuters on Monday Yeltsin's heart was all but back to normal and a should not pose any special problems.

"Based on the reports I'm getting, it would appear his cardiac function has been virtually restored to normal," DeBakey said. Yeltsin's recovery was "right on schedule" and the surgery would not leave him susceptible to infections such as a cold.
"It should make him more resistant," DeBakey said.
He added the cold was "transient and self-limited" but doctors would keep an eye on it. "Any cold should be taken seriously because it can develop into other things," he said.
DeBakey said he did not think the president's return to work had contributed to his catching cold. "He promised me he would be a good patient and I think he has been," said DeBakey, 88.
He said he would likely visit Yeltsin again in the spring when he was to attend a medical meeting in Russia.
